songs.title: The Blower's Turn (Sixteen to the Minute)
songs.performance_context: Sung by pairs of dwellers turning the hand-crank ventilation fan during surface storm alerts
songs.lyrics:
Left hand pull and right hand push / The snow is heavy on the bush / The black cloud sits upon the hill / The wheel must turn or blood will chill.

One for the coal that's in the fire / Two for the watchman on the wire / Three for the baby in the wool / Four for the belly nearly full.

Turn the iron, oil the sleeve / In the ash we learn to breathe.

songs.title: The Four Colors of the Sky
songs.performance_context: Recited by children in the Picket Schoolroom to memorize radiation and chemical hazard indicators
songs.lyrics:
White sky, snow is clean / Yellow sky, boil the green / Violet sky, run below / Black sky, let nobody go.

If the rain tastes like tin / Bolt the iron door within / If the pond is shining blue / Turn your boots and run on through.

songs.title: The Drowned Locks of Tessarat
songs.performance_context: Sung by the Ash-Sea skiff rowers while towing timber barges across the flooded lowlands
songs.lyrics:
The water rose above the sills / Before the bells had done their toll / The sapper dropped the lock-gate pins / And saved the winter wheat in whole.

Oh Morozov, the water's deep / Where forty cottages did stand / But in the cold forty below / We hold your shovel in our hand.

Row the ash and pull the sweep / The drowned church is fast asleep.

songs.title: Lullaby for a Cold Bunk
songs.performance_context: Sung by mothers in bunk room 4 when the turbine shuts down for nocturnal battery conservation
songs.lyrics:
Close your eyes, the light is dim / Fyodor stoked the boiler rim / Warm your feet against the brick / Listen to the geophone click.

Father's on the surface mast / Counting till the storm is past / When the winter winds are done / We will see the yellow sun.

Sleep my quiet, sleep my lamb / Safe behind the granite dam.

songs.title: The Anvil's Answer
songs.performance_context: Chanted by Master Oleg and his striker while drawing out hot alloy plowshares
songs.lyrics:
Strike the red! / Save the bread! / Strike the white! / Warm the night!

Cut the leaf spring from the lorry / We've no time to weep or worry / Hammer cold and hammer hot / Iron forgives what men cannot.

One strike true! / Two strikes through! / Bring the tongs and plunge it blue!

songs.title: The Baker's Third
songs.performance_context: Sung in the mess hall while waiting for the evening hard-tack biscuit distribution
songs.lyrics:
A third of rye, a third of peat / A third of alder from the street / Sift it fine through copper wire / Bake it hard upon the fire!

It breaks the tooth, it fills the gut / It keeps the hungry mouth right shut / If you drop it on your toe / You will limp for weeks in snow!

songs.title: The Song of the Brass Ring
songs.performance_context: Sung on the anniversary of Dr. Vel's vigil during the lighting of the clinic tallow candles
songs.lyrics:
She carried thirty-one upon her tongue / And spoke them quiet while the lantern hung / She did not reach for water or for bread / But held the brass ring till her fingers bled.

Oh Sonya, keep the little key / And let the sick dweller go free / The medicine chest is open wide / With thirty-one names carved inside.

songs.title: Eleven Kilometers on the Wire
songs.performance_context: Muttered by couriers while pacing between surface marker posts in blinding whiteouts
songs.lyrics:
Glove on the cable, boot in the drift / Ten more minutes to finish the shift / Post forty-two, post forty-three / Nothing to hear and nothing to see.

Keep the oilcloth dry and tight / Kerosene lantern burning bright / If you drop the wire, boy / The snow will have another toy.

songs.title: The Weight of the Salt
songs.performance_context: Sung by market porters while carrying salt sacks to Harlan's counting table
songs.lyrics:
A gram of salt for an inch of thread / A liter of brine for a loaf of bread / If you want the boots from the dead man's feet / Bring twenty nails from the furnace street.

Harlan sits with his balance true / He doesn't love me and he don't love you / But he keeps his thumbs right off the brass / And lets the winter barter pass.

songs.title: The Chisel's Bite
songs.meter: Free Meter Chant with Stone Mallet Strikes
songs.performance_context: Sung softly by Sister Mara in the granite crypt while carving dweller epitaphs
songs.lyrics:
Name by name / Cut the stone / In the dark / Flesh and bone.

Not a hero, not a king / Just the hand that turned the ring / Eight hundred names along the wall / The cold rock remembers all.

Rest your head, your watch is done / Beneath the stone we wait the sun.

songs.title: The Green Needle
songs.performance_context: Sung when the first winter rye shoots poke through the bone-ash peat beds in the sub-level greenhouse
songs.lyrics:
A little green needle in black dirt born / Under the yellow wire light this morn / Drink from the pipe where the charcoal sits / Rise from the gravel in tiny bits.

Grow for the flour, grow for the pot / Better than all of the goods we bought / A green blade growing in forty below / Tells the dead earth it is time to grow.

songs.title: Five Fathoms Down
songs.performance_context: Chanted by the hand-pump crew aboard the salvage barge while feeding air hoses down to the divers
songs.lyrics:
Crank the pump and watch the gauge / We're cutting through the iron cage / Five fathoms down in the acid foam / The Sovereign sits in her drowned home.

Bring up the crates of potassium foil / Bring up the drums of machine-head oil / We'll take what the lords of the war laid deep / And give it to children before they sleep.

songs.title: Ten Little Dwellers
songs.performance_context: Chanted by children jumping over a frayed telegraph cable in the main corridor
songs.lyrics:
Ten little dwellers sitting in a line / One ate the red snow, then there were nine.
Nine little dwellers working at the gate / One dropped his breather, then there were eight.
Eight little dwellers under boiler seven / One turned the valve wrong, now he's in heaven.
Seven little dwellers baking sawdust sticks / One burnt the oven, then there were six.
Six little dwellers learning how to dive / One tore his rubber suit, then there were five.
Five little dwellers tapping on the floor / Turn around, jump around, lock the heavy door!

songs.title: The Falling Stars of Station Zero
songs.performance_context: Broadcast over 88.4 MHz Pirate Free-Net during the Harrow-4 orbital decay pass
songs.lyrics:
The stars are falling from the shelf / The satellite is by itself / It traveled forty thousand miles / To land upon our slag-heap piles.

Don't fear the fire in the night / It has no fuse, it has no spite / Just heavy iron coming home / Through eight miles of the burning dome.

songs.title: The Slate on the Track
songs.performance_context: Sung by the Picket School students and foundry workers during the Article 4 rail strike
songs.lyrics:
Lay the shovels down, boys, lay the shovels down / No child shall feed the blast furnace in this town / We'll take the frost upon our face, we'll take the biting cold / But we will not buy our winter heat with children twelve years old.

Inscribe the slate! / Open the gate! / The law is carved, the people wait!

songs.title: The Anthem of the Open Lock
songs.performance_context: Sung by the combined assembly of Tessarat during the ten-year canal reopening ceremony
songs.lyrics:
The lock is clear! The water flows! / The river runs where no one goes! / Ten years of night, ten years of ash / Dissolve beneath the water's splash!

To all who starved, to all who wept / To all the quiet vows we kept: / The grass is green on Morozov's hill / The Valley lives and labor will!

Ring the iron bell! Let the whistles blow! / Out of the shadow, into the glow!
